title: shared-thread canon commits deadlock under intentd auto-ingest; the guard names the file, not the culprit
body:
A canon-carrying commit on a shared thread passes only when THAT THREAD'S ATTACHMENTS ARE COHERENT WITH GIT ACROSS ALL NODES -- and with a running intentd auto-ingesting disk edits, one node's dirty `parity/tools/` file silently blocks every other node's canon commit on that thread, through a file none of them is editing.

## The mechanism, measured on ST0056 on 2026-09-01

An attachment's bytes are stored in the thread's canon extract (`intent/.canon/st/<ST>.json`). `intent st attach --from` regenerates that extract from the STORE. The store is SSOT, and a running intentd (pid 62022 this session) AUTO-INGESTS a disk edit to any attachment into the store on its own. So the extract a node regenerates names the STORE's UNION of every dirty-and-ingested attachment on that thread -- including bytes committed by nobody yet.

`canon_commit_check.sh` then refuses the commit two ways, and together they are a trap:

- Commit the extract, and it names bytes git does not carry (a peer's ingested-but-uncommitted attachment) -> `ADDS N -- the index names bytes it does not contain`.
- Commit the attachment WITHOUT the extract, and HEAD's canon still names the OLD sha for the file whose bytes you just changed -> same guard, other direction.

So there is no ordering of separate per-node commits that closes: the only commit that passes carries EVERY dirty-and-ingested attachment on the thread, across all nodes, in one window. The guard is correct every time; the estate is nonetheless deadlocked while more than one node holds a dirty attachment on the same thread.

Observed: four nodes (ic x2 files, cc x1, vc x1) each holding a dirty ST0056 `parity/tools/` attachment; each node's canon commit refused. Resolved only by vc taking a single combined commit (`11528266`: five paths, three authors, canon) -- explicitly because canon could not be split.

## The part that makes it a defect rather than a constraint: the guard names the FILE but not the CULPRIT

A blocked node is told `ADDS 1 -- parity/tools/canon_race_check.sh`. Reaching the actionable conclusion "wait for a peer" took THREE inferences the guard does not supply: whose file it is (`git log` -> cc), that the peer holds it dirty (`git status` -> worktree 38adff91 != HEAD 9d2c5f1a), and that intentd had ingested it (the store names bytes on disk but not in git). A refusal that cannot say WHO TO WAIT FOR is a deadlock with extra steps, and the victim does archaeology to discover they are a victim. This is the fixable half: the guard, or `intent doctor`, could name the owning peer, the dirty status, and "committed by nobody -- coordinate", turning archaeology into a one-line instruction.

## What this issue does NOT establish

- Whether the trap reaches threads OTHER than ST0056. Not measured. ST0056 is the hot shared thread; a thread with a single active writer would not exhibit it, but that is reasoning, not a measurement.
- What happens with intentd STOPPED. Not measured. The auto-ingest is the mechanism that turns a peer's dirty file into your blocker; without it the extract should name only committed + your-own bytes, but this is untested.

Both are cheap and neither is done. Do not read the ST0056 measurement as an estate-wide claim.

## Evidence

- 2026-09-01, HEAD progressing through `11528266`; gate line `canon-commit: ADDS 1 of 320 attachment(s) examined -- the index names bytes it does not contain: ST0056/parity/tools/canon_race_check.sh`.
- `canon_race_check.sh` worktree `38adff91` vs HEAD `9d2c5f1a`; last two commits cc's (`130b0aa6`, `649cb542`).
- intentd running, pid 62022, `/Users/matts/.local/bin/intentd`.
- Resolution: single combined commit `11528266` (ic's two 0205 `.sh`, cc's `canon_race_check.sh`, vc's `acceptance.md`, canon), authored by vc with per-file attribution.

## Relation to prior findings

This is the mechanism behind the coherence layer dc named (store / git / index -- contention is routable with a private index, COHERENCE is not). It also sits beside 0206 (concurrent same-thread store writes silently clobber): 0206 is two writers racing one record; this is N writers each holding a dirty attachment, surfaced by the byte-guard rather than lost silently. Measured and authored by ic; resolution and the "author dispositions it" hand-back by vc; cc's file was the trigger.
